summary:
Turn 60 closed the codec finding's open consequence with a second scenario on the same obligation.

What was observed locally. Two commands are written back to back: one with a 70000-byte value (beyond the two-byte length field) and one small command. After decoding the first (which recovers only 4464 of its value bytes), the decoder reads the next command from the leftover payload and produces garbage: op 197, an arbitrary key (about -3.6e18) and a 53198-byte value, with 12341 bytes still in the buffer. So the truncation does not only shorten one value — it destroys the framing of everything after it in the same stream, which is how batches and the durable command log are written.

Product. A second artifact on the same unit (unit-C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire): a new plan and harness where the prerequisite prints the two written commands and the total wire size, and the result asserts second_matches == true on the stream-shift event, with the stream identity correlating the two, the existing codec binding and the same grounding. The plan records that concatenated Command marshallings are exactly how batches and the durable record append commands, and the uncertainty keeps the reader-side reaction (what replicaListener does with the shifted stream, e.g. an unknown message type after the framing is lost) outside this check rather than assumed.

State. Audit spec moved to version 13; the C10 finding now has two scenarios (the value truncation, reviewed and confirmed, and this stream-shift consequence awaiting the trusted runner and a fresh correspondence review), the map handoff for C10 is accepted, and the nine earlier settled claims plus the two paused candidates are untouched. The only visible administrative item remains the scope issue on the superseded C1 artifact. No requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
